sections.name: File setup, project, capture, source
sections.title: Test setup and fake source
sections.what: Imports the test tools and creates a made-up project, a made-up passage, a capture record and a source record.
sections.why: The file header and the passage text say this is a synthetic test passage, not research evidence.
sections.watch_out: The fake addresses use an invalid domain, so no real site should be contacted.

sections.name: extracted
sections.title: Fake AI extraction result
sections.what: Provides a made-up AI reply containing two facts, an owner and a technology, both pointing to the same passage.
sections.why: Replaces the real AI call so the test runs without outside services.
sections.watch_out: If the expected extraction format changes, this fake reply must be updated too.

sections.name: register
sections.title: Tests for collection behaviour
sections.what: Three tests. One checks that different claims and capture dates produce different source IDs. One checks that a failing source does not stop the next source. One checks that cancelling keeps the full scope and that resuming reuses saved text without another web request.
sections.why: The test names state the rules being protected.
sections.watch_out: The resume test counts web requests. Adding a retry to the capture step would make this test fail.

summary: Automated tests that check the research collector handles duplicate identifiers, failing sources, cancellation and resuming correctly.
purpose: Protects the collection behaviour from regressions when the collector changes.
why: Reason not stated in the file beyond the test names, which describe the rules being checked.
how: Builds a made-up project and passage, then runs the collector with fake capture and fake extraction services. Checks counts, statuses and saved snapshots. Contains three tests.
inputs: Fixed fake data written inside the file. No outside inputs.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each of the three tests.
risks: Fake data and fake services cannot show how real web pages or the real AI behave.
debug: Run this file and read the first failing assertion. Check the status names the collector writes, and check that the saved snapshots still record each stage.
